ecological_question: Does the timescale over which past state remains predictive depend on the ecological state dimension being measured?
working_hypothesis: Coarse persistence or recorded-state variables integrate longer ecological histories, whereas quantitative meadow condition is dominated more strongly by the immediately previous state.
not_yet_identified: Whether state dimension itself causes the different apparent memory horizon.
Whether the contrast instead reflects model family, response distribution, monitoring protocol, species, habitat, or noise structure.

prospective_confirmatory_design.candidate_requirement: A response-unopened repeated monitoring system with both a variable coarse presence/persistence state and a quantitative condition state measured on the same stable sampling units over at least five target years.
prospective_confirmatory_design.split: Identical strict walk-forward target-year splits for both state dimensions.
prospective_confirmatory_design.baseline: Same response-independent site/time covariates and stable-unit identity within each state-specific model.
prospective_confirmatory_design.older_history_increment: Predeclared older-history mean, slope and history length; no post-outcome feature retuning.
prospective_confirmatory_design.support_rule: For each state dimension separately, older history is supported only if it wins at least 60% of target years, has negative median paired loss delta versus lag1, and one-sided paired year-level sign-flip p<0.05.
prospective_confirmatory_design.primary_prediction: Older history will satisfy the support rule for the coarse state more often than for quantitative condition.
forbidden: Selecting thresholds after seeing outcomes to manufacture a coarse state.
Changing history features or support rules by state after outcome access.
Comparing raw effect magnitudes across incompatible loss functions as if directly commensurate.
Calling the current Tampa/NPS contrast causal confirmation.
